titulo: The door: the Telegram bot, with a single owner
lead: Telegram is the simplest door: you create the bot in two minutes and get a token. That token is the key to the door. Whoever has the token controls the bot, and anyone can send a message to a bot. That's why this lesson is half creating and half protecting.
objetivo: create the bot with @BotFather, keep the token only in the .env, and set the assistant to respond only to you.

aprende.t: Why the token stays only in the .env and out of Git
How the channel talks to Telegram (long-polling)
Why the bot needs to accept only the owner

hero_alt: Hands holding a phone with a messaging app open on a conversation.

nos.detalhe: Telegram's official bot that creates bots. You send /newbot, choose the name and the @username (which ends in bot), and get the token.
A string of numbers and letters. Whoever has the token controls the bot. It goes only into the .env (or the encrypted vault the plan provides for), never into the code, a screenshot, or a commit.
The channel keeps asking Telegram whether a new message has arrived. It doesn't need a public address. It splits replies longer than 4096 characters and refuses to start without a token, on purpose.
Anyone who finds your bot's @ can send it a message. Without a list of who can talk, anyone can chat with your Jarvis and use its tools.

secoes.volta: Replies go back to the same chat
secoes.legenda: INTELECTO was designed for one user. A Jarvis with access to your machine is powerful, and that is exactly why it deserves care.

secoes.titulo: Create and protect, step by step

texto: In Telegram, search for @BotFather (the official one, with the verified badge) and send /newbot.
Choose the name that appears in the chat and the @username, which must end in bot. It replies with the token.

exemplo.texto: Use the name from your meu-jarvis.md. The @username can be the name + _bot.

texto: Paste the token on a line of the .env in the project folder, as you learned in step 1.
Check that .env is in .gitignore. Bots find keys exposed on GitHub within minutes.

exemplo.texto: The token doesn't appear in any file other than .env.

texto: When you build it (lesson 4), ask the agent to make the bot answer only your Telegram user and ignore everyone else.
In the vault (lesson 7) you'll see why this matters even more when the assistant runs commands.

exemplo.texto: The bot answers only my Telegram user; messages from other people are ignored and logged.

texto: A token in a screenshot, in a group, or in a commit is a leaked token. Don't delete it and hope: generate a new one in @BotFather and swap it in the .env.
The old token stops working, and whoever got it loses access.

exemplo.texto: /mybots → choose the bot → API Token → generate a new one.

secoes.sub: Replace the text between < > with your token. Never paste the token here in the course or in a chat.

abas.html:
grep shows the .env line in .gitignore.

git status doesn't list .env.

Searching for the start of the token finds nothing outside .env.

If git status shows ?? .env, the line is missing from .gitignore: add it before any commit.

If the search finds the token in another file, delete it there and generate a new token in @BotFather.

exercicios.texto: Create the bot in @BotFather with /newbot and keep the token in the .env of the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: you have the token and it doesn't appear in any file other than .env (the search in the third block finds nothing).

perguntas.p: Where can the bot's token appear?
opcoes: In the README, as a reminder.
In the team group, so everyone can test.
Only in .env (or in the encrypted vault), outside Git.
In the code, to make things easier.
perguntas.explica: Whoever has the token controls the bot. It lives only in .env, which is in .gitignore; anywhere else, count it as leaked and replace it.

perguntas.p: Why does the bot need a list of who is allowed to talk to it?
opcoes: Because anyone can message a bot and would end up using your assistant.
perguntas.explica: A Telegram bot is public to anyone who finds its @. Without the list, a stranger can chat with your Jarvis and use its tools.

perguntas.p: Your token showed up in a screenshot you posted. Which is the right move?
opcoes: Delete the post and move on.
Generate a new token in @BotFather and swap it in .env.
perguntas.explica: Deleting doesn't undo the leak. Generating a new token invalidates the old one; whoever copied it loses access.
